ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there are special markings or behaviors near x=1, x=2, and x=3. At x=1, the curve on the left ends with a solid point, while another segment of the curve on the right begins at the same x value with an open circle, and the y values of these two points are different. At x=2, a vertical dashed line is drawn, and the curve extends infinitely upward and downward near the dashed line, appearing as a vertical asymptote. At x=3, there is an open circle, and the curves on the left and right connect at the same y value, but this point is not filled in. Reasoning: A jump discontinuity requires that both the left and right limits exist and are finite, but that the left and right limits are not equal. At x=1, the left and right limits are finite but different, so it is a jump discontinuity; x=2 is an infinite discontinuity; at x=3 the left and right limits are the same, so it is a removable discontinuity. Therefore, the jump discontinuity occurs at x=1.

method.method_draft: First describe the visible graph features: note the labeled x-values 1, 2, and 3 where something special happens. At x=1, the left-hand piece ends at a filled dot at one y-value, while the next piece begins with an open circle at a different y-value. At x=2, there is a dashed vertical line and the graph tends vertically, indicating an infinite discontinuity. At x=3, there is an open circle on the curve where the left and right pieces meet at the same y-value. Then apply the definition of jump discontinuity: compare the left-hand and right-hand limits at each candidate x-value; a jump occurs when both one-sided limits are finite but unequal. Only x=1 satisfies this, so the x-value is 1.

method.method_draft: First scan the graph for visual discontinuity markers. Identify three marker types: at x=1 there is a filled point and a separate open point vertically above it on the same x-value; at x=2 there is a vertical dashed asymptote; at x=3 there is a single open hole on an otherwise connecting pair of curve pieces. Use the standard graph-symbol classification: a filled/open mismatch at the same x with different heights indicates the function switches from one finite branch value to another, which is a jump; a dashed vertical asymptote indicates an infinite discontinuity; a lone hole where approaching branches agree indicates a removable discontinuity. Therefore select x=1 as the jump discontinuity.
